text:
Maya: kicking off a concise plan for tenant-windowed canaries. AcmeCorp and two SMB partners asked for scheduled opt-in windows + strong rollback guarantees. I sketched a safe flow, want quick alignment on stage sizes, telemetry, and customer controls.

Oliver: high level ok. propose smaller initial blast to limit blast radius: 2% -> 10% -> 25%. keep 2x monitoring cadence on first stage.

Priya: telemetry gates: p99 latency increase > 150ms OR p95 > baseline+120ms, 5xx rate > +0.4pp, and quality regression on our golden prompt set > 2% absolute. include cost-per-token soft-threshold at +25%.

Quinn: fallback chain idea: 1) immediate switch to lightweight CPU-safe variant in same region (same API), 2) spill to standby region, 3) serve last-known-good cached response (if prefix match), 4) synthetic graceful reply with retry token. log fallback_reason and fallback_step.

Ravi: about tenant windows: support start/end schedules (timezone aware) and business-hours-only option. also need per-tenant pause/resume without a full flag churn. use cohort-based rules in rollout service.

Maya: agree on cohort-based flags. we should not create per-tenant flags. one rollout id with tenant whitelist and scheduled windows. also add an "always-skip" enterprise list.

Priya: monitoring cadence: stage-1 -> check at 5, 15, 30 min; advance only after two green checks. stage-2 -> check every 15 min, need 3 green checks. auto-rollback if any critical gate trips; human confirmation required to re-enable.

Oliver: deployment ops: pre-warm caches and allocate a 10% reserved capacity buffer for the canary pool. rolling update cap: max 10% of a pool at a time to avoid correlated cold-starts.

Quinn: quality check: run shadow A/B for opt-ins (customer chooses A vs baseline). for non-opt-ins, keep single-variant path. collect human-review flags for top 30 candidate failures per hour if thresholded by heuristic scorer.

Ravi: customer notifications: Console toggle + schedule UI, email to tenant admin at each stage start/advance/rollback. include link to rollback button in the email and a short explanation of what fallback means.

Priya: instrumentation: tag every request with rollout_id, tenant_id, and cohort_label. store sampled prompts at 0.5% for 14 days. emit metric rollout.stage.change and rollout.fallback.count with reason label.

Maya: escalation and kill-switch: auto-open a P1 to SRE on critical gate trip. provide Console single-click kill and API endpoint POST /api/v1/rollouts/{id}/abort. ops-bot: please schedule staged runbook email to #product 10m before start.

ops-bot: preflight: capacity check passed for us-east-1 pool. scheduled start 2025-09-22T09:00Z. will post reminder 10m prior.

Oliver: one more: add a hysteresis window for cost spikes — if cost_delta > 25% for 30m, reduce traffic fraction by 50% and notify.

Quinn: add synthetic traffic generator to populate baselines in quieter regions. also compare tokenization patterns vs baseline to detect degenerate prompts.

Maya: decisions summary to lock into PM spec: 1) staged sizes: 2% -> 10% -> 25% 2) hold windows and check counts as described 3) telemetry gates: p99/p95 latency, 5xx, eval regression, cost_delta 4) fallback: cpu-variant -> region spill -> cache -> polite degrade 5) cohort-based single-flag with tenant schedule + always-skip list 6) kill-switch: Console+API+auto-pager 7) instrumentation: rollout_id/tenant_id tags + sampled prompts.

Priya: I'll add precise thresholds and alerting rules to the doc.

Ravi: I'll mock the Console toggle and schedule UI and drop screenshots.

Oliver: ops acceptance: will add prewarm and reserve buffer steps to deployment checklist.

Maya: thanks. please add acceptance criteria by EOD tomorrow so I can finalize PRD. low-priority ask: include a short email template for tenant admins when you drop your UI mock.

Quinn: noted, adding a short runbook and the human-review flow.

ops-bot: reminder: preflight notice will be sent to #product 2025-09-22T08:50Z.
